page: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-96 is a graphics-optimized server featuring eight NVIDIA L4 GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing a total of 192 GB of VRAM. The system is powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor with 96 dedicated vCPUs, consisting of 48 physical cores and 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 2.2 GHz. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, translating to 4.0 GB per core, and does not include local storage.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile. While single-core CPU metrics are weak, placing in the bottom 25% for stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests, the server excels in multi-core and memory-intensive operations. Multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng is strong, and memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 4211.44 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 208.49 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Most notably, the system achieves top-tier performance in LLM inference prompt processing, handling 11350.23 tokens/sec for small models and 294.28 tokens/sec for large models.

The primary tradeoff of the g2-standard-96 is its modest single-threaded performance, as evidenced by lower scores in single-threaded compression and text processing. However, the high density of eight dedicated GPUs combined with 96 vCPUs offers exceptional qualitative cost efficiency for parallelized workloads. The resource density makes it highly optimized for multi-threaded execution and GPU-bound tasks, offsetting the lower single-core efficiency.

This server is designed for demanding workloads such as large language model inference, multi-threaded data processing, and GPU-accelerated compute tasks. It is also well-suited for high-throughput database operations, as demonstrated by strong Redis SET performance of 63.66 million operations per second, and parallelized scientific simulations.

It also exhibits high memory bandwidth and strong Redis performance. Qualitatively, the high density of GPUs and dedicated vCPUs makes it a cost-efficient choice for parallelized, GPU-bound workloads rather than single-threaded applications. The g2-standard-96 is highly suited for LLM inference, multi-threaded data processing, and GPU-accelerated compute tasks.
